verdict.rationale: React's own docs say it can stream HTML on the server while data is still being fetched, progressively filling in content (react-docs-6). This implies a loading-UI mechanism for server-loaded data. The pack never names Suspense, resource/`use`-style primitives, or fallback UIs, and async data-fetching components are attributed to frameworks that implement the architecture (react-docs-7). Missing for 10: explicit documentation of Suspense boundaries and fallbacks, a resource/`use` primitive for treating fetched data as reactive state, client-side loading-state handling, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
